description: A structured or semi-structured collection of data published for reuse, typically available as downloadable files (CSV, JSON, XML, etc.) or via an API; raw blog posts, articles, or single static documents do not count.
examples: COVID-19 Cases and Deaths by County, United States
EPA Air Quality Measurements - Monitoring Stations

fields.name: title
fields.description: The dataset's name as displayed at the top of its page, usually a short descriptive phrase.

fields.name: description
fields.description: A short paragraph summarizing what the dataset contains, its scope, and how it was collected; usually in plain prose below the title.
fields.example: State-level monthly mean temperature values (degrees F) for the contiguous United States, compiled from NOAA station data.

fields.name: publisher
fields.description: The organization or agency that authored or hosts the dataset, often shown as a logo or 'Source' label.

fields.name: publication_date
fields.description: The date the dataset was first released or published, commonly labeled 'Release Date' or 'Published'.

fields.name: last_updated
fields.description: The date the dataset was most recently revised; often labeled 'Last Updated', 'Modified', or 'Refreshed'.

fields.name: formats
fields.description: The available file formats for download, typically shown as badges or links (e.g., CSV, JSON, XML, XLSX).

fields.name: license
fields.description: The usage license under which the dataset is released (e.g., CC-BY 4.0, Public Domain, ODbL), often shown with a license name or icon.

fields.name: download_url
fields.description: Direct link to the primary downloadable file or landing page for the dataset, usually labeled 'Download' or shown as the resource URL.

fields.name: doi
fields.description: A Digital Object Identifier assigned to the dataset, often labeled 'DOI' and presented as a clickable link.
